summary: CCC-era 100-foot tower near Barton in Colbert County, AL, completed 1942; NHLR-registered 2009. No staffing or current access source found.

facts.design: 100-foot International Derrick tower with a 7-by-7-foot cab

events.note: Completed in 1942; a July 1942 Alabama Journal item reports completion, and the Register says built in 1942 as the last CCC-completed tower in Alabama
Registered December 6, 2009 as US 846, AL 24, nominated by Thomas Kaufmann

evidence.supports: built 1942; last fire tower completed by the CCC in Alabama
evidence.quote: The last fire tower to be completed by the CCC in Alabama, Mountain Mills Lookout Tower was built in 1942.
It is a 100' International Derrick tower with 7'x7' cab.

evidence.supports: administered by the Alabama Forestry Commission
July 1942 Alabama Journal item: completed near Barton by the state conservation department
evidence.quote: has been completed by the Alabama Conservation Department
The new observation post is a 100-foot steel tower.
four additional ones are under construction

evidence.supports: CCC built 61 lookout towers in Alabama by 1942
evidence.quote: the CCC had built 1,800 miles of roads, 61 lookout towers

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register attributes the tower to the CCC; the 1942 Alabama Journal excerpt credits the state forestry division and does not mention the CCC. Both point to 1942 completion, so the Register's CCC attribution is reported as the Register's claim

sources.title: Mountain Mills (quoting the Alabama Journal, July 1, 1942)

notes_for_editor: Thin record: the Register and one 1942 newspaper excerpt quoted by Forest Lookouts. No staffing, access or present-condition source found; the story says so. The Register calls the tower the last CCC-completed fire tower in Alabama; the 1942 excerpt does not mention the CCC. The record's height_m 30.5 matches the Register's 100-foot figure, so it was not changed. The name Mountain Mills also belongs to a historic cotton-mill community (Wikipedia, Colbert County history); no source tied the tower to the mill, so none is claimed. Forest Lookouts' Alabama list also has a separate Barton Knob (Mt Mills) entry, which was not checked and should not be conflated.
